questions.q: On both AKS and EKS, in what order does a cluster upgrade happen?
options: Node pools/groups upgrade first, then the control plane
The control plane upgrades first, and can run one version ahead of the nodes for a while before they're upgraded
Everything upgrades simultaneously in a single atomic step
Only the control plane is ever upgraded; nodes are always replaced with new VMs instead
questions.explain: Both platforms upgrade the control plane first, independently of the nodes, enabling a staged rollout rather than an all-at-once cutover.

questions.q: What does draining a node actually do before it's upgraded or removed?
options: Immediately deletes all Pods on the node with no rescheduling
Cordons the node as unschedulable, then gracefully evicts its Pods so they can reschedule onto other nodes before the node is removed
Only stops new Pods from being created, but leaves running ones in place indefinitely
Reboots the node without affecting its Pods
questions.explain: A drain marks a node unschedulable and evicts Pods gracefully, giving them a chance to reschedule elsewhere before the node is actually removed — avoiding all Pods on that node dying at once.

questions.q: What does a PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable: 2 do during a cluster upgrade?
options: It prevents the upgrade from ever running
It prevents the upgrade process from draining a node if doing so would drop that workload's running replica count below 2
It guarantees exactly 2 replicas will always exist, even outside of upgrades
It forces all upgrades to happen within 2 minutes
questions.explain: PodDisruptionBudget caps how many replicas can be unavailable during a voluntary disruption like a drain — the upgrade process respects it, pausing rather than violating the budget.

questions.q: Why would Northbridge configure an AKS maintenance window for Saturday mornings rather than letting upgrades apply at any time?
options: AKS requires maintenance windows to be configured before any cluster can run
It restricts when automatic upgrades are applied to a low-traffic period, reducing the chance an upgrade-related disruption affects customers
Maintenance windows only affect billing, not upgrade timing
Saturday mornings are the only time az aks upgrade can be run manually
questions.explain: A planned maintenance window restricts automatic upgrades to a chosen time range, letting a team pick a low-traffic period rather than risk disruption during peak hours.

questions.q: What risk does skipping node draining (e.g. just deleting nodes outright) introduce during an upgrade?
options: No risk — Kubernetes always reschedules Pods instantly with zero downtime regardless
Every Pod on that node is terminated at once with no guarantee enough capacity exists elsewhere to absorb them immediately
It only affects StatefulSets, never Deployments
It makes the upgrade run faster with no other consequence
questions.explain: Without draining, Pods on a removed node are simply lost at once rather than gracefully evicted and rescheduled, risking a capacity crunch or a visible outage.
